quote: It is conjectured [R. Guy] that all finitely-specified octal games have ultimately periodic Nim-value sequences
note: The conjecture appears in "Winning Ways for Your Mathematical Plays" by Berlekamp, Conway, and Guy (1982), the first major publication where the periodicity problem for octal games is documented. Earlier foundational work on octal games was published by Guy and Smith in 1956 ("The G-Values of Various Games"), but the specific periodicity question was not explicitly formulated until 1982. The problem is attributed to Richard Guy.
